description: Renovate tracks three things here: the upstream Omnigent release pinned in nix/source.nix (custom regex manager), the flake inputs in flake.lock (weekly lock file maintenance only), and the GitHub Actions used by .github/workflows.

gitIgnoredAuthors: .github/workflows/renovate-hashes.yml pushes a fixup commit (regenerated hashes and re-synced lockfile pins) onto renovate/** branches. Renovate treats a branch carrying a commit by anyone but itself as human-edited and stops updating it, so without this entry a newer upstream release would never reach an already-open PR.

packageRules.description: Flake inputs track branches (nixos-unstable, home-manager master) that move daily. Only the weekly lockFileMaintenance PR (`nix flake update`) refreshes them; per-input digest PRs would be constant noise.

Upstream Omnigent releases. The PR only rewrites `version` + `commit`; CI (renovate-hashes.yml) regenerates the fixed-output hashes and re-syncs the pnpm/Python pins from upstream's lockfiles on the branch, then check.yml builds and tests it. Always merged by a human. Upstream also tags release candidates (v0.21.0rc1) and daily builds (v0.22.0.dev20261107); pep440 versioning (set in the annotation) treats those as pre-releases, and allowedVersions keeps only final X.Y.Z releases even if the current pin were ever a pre-release.
prBodyNotes: Fixed-output hashes and the pins copied from upstream's lockfiles (pnpm, cel-python, pythonPins) are regenerated by the `renovate hashes` workflow, which pushes a fixup commit to this branch. Wait for that commit and a green `check` run before merging. Review `nix/source.nix` in the final diff: a pythonPins version change may mean a pin can be dropped, or a new one is needed.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions: SHA-pinned (tag in a trailing comment), grouped into one weekly PR, and held for 7 days after release so a compromised tag has time to be noticed.

customManagers.description: Upstream Omnigent release in nix/source.nix. The match spans the `# renovate:` annotation through the `commit` line, so the version (currentValue) and the tag's commit (currentDigest, which the github-tags datasource resolves) are rewritten in one edit. It stops short of the hashes, which no string substitution can derive: scripts/update-hashes.sh regenerates those in CI. extractVersionTemplate strips the tag's `v` so `version` stays bare (`tag = "v${version}"`). The {1,6} line bound keeps the match from running past `commit`.
